title: PR #142: Idempotent Webhook Ingestion & Lease Recovery

overview.whole_task: We're making Stripe and GitHub webhooks safe against duplicate retries and surfacing live dedup status in the [[payments-admin-console|Payments Admin Console]] so support can see skipped events and [[claimed-lease|active locks]].
overview.this_pr_part: This PR builds the backend half: the [[idempotency-store|Postgres lock table]] and [[webhook-router|`/webhooks/:provider`]] guard so retries stop double-charging right away—the [[payments-admin-console|Admin Console]] manual-retry button comes in the next PR.

footprint.label: Idempotency store
footprint.change: New [[idempotency-store|Postgres lock store]] that claims, finishes and frees one webhook event at a time.

footprint.label: Webhook route
footprint.change: [[webhook-router|`/webhooks/:provider`]] now checks the lock before it calls `WebhookDispatcher`.

edges.label: dispatch() only after a won claim

ship_facts.schema_migrations: Adds the `webhook_idempotency_keys` table, so run the migration before the new API rolls out.
ship_facts.api_contracts: `/webhooks/:provider` now answers duplicates with `200 deduplicated` instead of running them again.
ship_facts.deploy_order: Migration first, then the API; old pods ignore the new table, so rolling back is safe.

overview.before_state: Whenever Stripe or GitHub retried a webhook, we ran `WebhookDispatcher` again and could charge a customer twice.
overview.after_state: Now `webhookRouter` locks `(provider, event_id)` in `PostgresIdempotencyStore` first and replies `200 OK` right away if we've already seen it.

visuals.caption: Here's the bigger [[payments-admin-console|Admin Console]] flow this backend powers: duplicate retries get a `200 deduplicated` badge (top right) while in-flight runs hold a [[claimed-lease|60s lock]].

concepts.what_it_is: Short 60-second lock timer we put on a webhook ID while a worker is running it.
how_it_works: **Crash recovery:** If a worker dies mid-request, `lease_expires_at` passes after 60s so the next retry can steal the lock and finish.
**Fast rollback:** If a handler throws normally, `releaseClaim()` deletes the lock right away instead of waiting 60s.
concepts.pr_impact: Brand-new concept introduced by this task so crashed workers never block retries forever.

concepts.what_it_is: New Postgres lock helper that tracks whether a `(provider, event_id)` webhook is running or done.
how_it_works: **One SQL round-trip:** Uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` so checking and locking happen together without race conditions.
**Crash recovery:** Uses a 60-second `CLAIMED` timer so another worker can take over if a pod dies mid-request.
concepts.pr_impact: Brand-new helper we build in Chapter 1 and plug into the route in Chapter 2.

concepts.what_it_is: Hands verified webhook payloads off to our billing and repo-sync handlers.
how_it_works: **Runs inline:** Executes right inside the `POST /webhooks/:provider` request with no background queue.
**On error:** Throws if a handler fails so Express returns `500` and the provider retries later.
**What it expects:** Assumes signature checks and dedup already happened before `dispatch()` runs.
concepts.pr_impact: We didn't touch its code—`webhookRouter` just skips calling it whenever `PostgresIdempotencyStore` says we already handled that event.

concepts.what_it_is: Express route that receives `POST /webhooks/:provider` calls from Stripe, GitHub, and Adyen.
how_it_works: **Where the ID comes from:** Checks the `x-webhook-id` header first and falls back to `req.body.id`.
**Error handling:** Uncaught errors bubble down into `webhookErrorHandler` at the bottom of the file.
concepts.pr_impact: Now rejects missing IDs with `400`, checks `PostgresIdempotencyStore` before running the webhook, and frees the lock if dispatch crashes.

concepts.what_it_is: Internal support dashboard that lists incoming Stripe and GitHub webhook deliveries and their status.
how_it_works: **Status badges:** Shows whether each delivery ran, failed, held a `CLAIMED` lock, or returned `200 deduplicated`.
concepts.pr_impact: Its frontend code isn't changed in this PR, but our new dedup statuses power its delivery badges.

chapters.title: Atomic Lease Store
chapters.summary: Sets up the [[idempotency-store|Postgres lock table]], types, and single-query claim check.

chapters.title: Webhook Guard & UI
chapters.summary: Adds finish/undo helpers, hooks the guard into [[webhook-router|`/webhooks/:provider`]], and checks the tests.

steps.title: Lock table and TypeScript types
steps.explanation: First we set up the `webhook_idempotency_keys` table and `IdempotencyStore` types that the rest of the PR uses.

rows: A worker is running this webhook right now until `lease_expires_at`.
We already finished this webhook, so future retries get skipped.

steps.title: Single-query claim check and [[claimed-lease|60s crash recovery]]
steps.explanation: Next we write `claimOrSkip()` in `PostgresIdempotencyStore` so only one worker can grab each event.

points.text: `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` only steals an existing row if it's still `CLAIMED` and [[claimed-lease|its 60s timer ran out]].
When Postgres updates zero rows, someone else is running or finished it, so we return `SKIP_IN_FLIGHT_OR_DONE`.

diff_highlights.title: Single-query lease steal
diff_highlights.explanation: Grabs a 60s `CLAIMED` row—or steals an expired one—in a single SQL query so two workers never race. Already `COMPLETED` rows update zero rows.

diff_highlights.title: Fail-open DB catch
diff_highlights.explanation: If Postgres throws, we return `PROCESS` anyway so a quick DB blip doesn't drop live customer webhooks.

callouts.text: Heads up: `catch` lets the webhook run when Postgres fails (`store.ts` L29)—check if billing webhooks should return `500` instead.
`lease_expires_at` uses app `Date.now()` (`L14`) while conflict checks use DB `NOW()` (`L22`), which can drift if clocks are off.

steps.title: Finish and undo helpers on the store
steps.explanation: Now we add `markCompleted()` and `releaseClaim()` onto `PostgresIdempotencyStore` so the route can finish or [[claimed-lease|undo a lock]].

rows: Marks the row `COMPLETED` so future retries skip it.
Deletes the `CLAIMED` row so the next retry can run.

steps.title: Hook the lock guard into [[webhook-router|/webhooks/:provider]]
steps.explanation: Here we register `PostgresIdempotencyStore` and wrap `WebhookDispatcher` inside `webhookRouter`.

visuals.caption: Even though we only touched backend SQL and Express here, this is how it shows up in the [[payments-admin-console|Admin Console]]: duplicates return `200 deduplicated` (top right) while active runs hold a [[claimed-lease|60s lock]].

callouts.text: If `releaseClaim()` throws during a DB outage inside `catch` (`webhooks.ts` L34), it'll swallow the original error from `WebhookDispatcher`.

diff_highlights.title: Validate ID & skip duplicates
diff_highlights.explanation: Grabs `x-webhook-id` (or `req.body.id`), returns `400` if it's missing, and replies `200 deduplicated` right away if [[idempotency-store|another worker owns or finished it]].

diff_highlights.title: Finalize or free lease on error
diff_highlights.explanation: Replaces the old unguarded `dispatchProviderWebhook` call: marks the key `COMPLETED` once `WebhookDispatcher` finishes, or deletes the `CLAIMED` row in `catch` so the next retry isn't stuck.

steps.title: Check unit tests (spots a broken mock test)
steps.explanation: Finally we look at the unit tests for duplicate skips and [[claimed-lease|expired locks]]—and catch a bug in the mock.

callouts.text: Bug in `webhook-dedup.test.ts` L7–14: the mock returns a row, so [[idempotency-store|`store.ts`]] actually returns `PROCESS` instead of skipping!

untested_gaps: Tests mock `db.query`, so our real `ON CONFLICT` SQL never runs against Postgres.
No route test checks missing `eventId` (`400`) or `releaseClaim()` when `WebhookDispatcher` throws.
